name: Shi Nengkeng
current_role: Reported founder and (as of 2015) chairman of Fujian Xunxing Group / Fujian SBS Zipper Science & Technology (SZSE: 002098), Jinjiang, Fujian; current role unverified
profile: Shi Nengkeng (施能坑) is reported as the founder of the Shi family's Xunxing Group in Jinjiang, Fujian, whose SBS brand grew from the Jinjiang Hualian Zipper Factory (1984) into one of China's largest zipper makers, listed in Shenzhen as 002098. Xunxing Group was the listed company's controlling shareholder. Little English-language information on him is available.
interesting_fact: The company's 'SBS' brand is said to stand for the brothers and sisters of the founding family. Xunxing also sponsors Jinjiang's CBA basketball club, the Fujian SBS Xunxing Sturgeons.
notes: Very low-profile private Chinese entrepreneur with almost no English coverage. Unofficial wiki mirrors name 'Nengkeng Shi' as founder/chairman, but I could not verify his current role from an official source (Baidu Baike was blocked). The SBS 'brothers and sisters' explanation comes from a search summary. The best route is likely via the listed company's investor relations (SZSE 002098).

name: Raghuram Shetty
current_role: Managing Director and co-promoter, Heranba Industries Ltd (NSE: HERANBA), Vapi, Gujarat
profile: Raghuram K. Shetty co-founded Heranba Industries in 1992 with his brother Sadashiv K. Shetty, who is chairman. Based in Vapi, Gujarat, Heranba grew into one of India's larger makers of crop-protection chemicals (synthetic pyrethroids, intermediates and formulations) and listed on the NSE/BSE in 2021. He remains MD, and the next generation now sits on the board.
interesting_fact: Heranba now has plants at Vapi and Sarigam and a greenfield site coming up at Saykha, Gujarat. In January 2026 it announced plans for a UAE subsidiary to make and trade crop-protection and nutrition chemicals.
notes: His profile is low-key and I found no personal social media or interviews. corporate@heranba.com is a company address, not a personal one. MarketScreener says he studied at the University of Mysore. That is unverified, so I left it out of the facts.

name: Yamunadutt Amilal Agrawal
current_role: Founder and Chairman (non-executive), Jindal Worldwide Ltd (NSE: JINDWORLD), Ahmedabad
profile: Dr Yamunadutt Agrawal founded Jindal Worldwide, an Ahmedabad textile group that calls itself one of India's largest denim makers. It also makes bottom-weight, shirting and yarn-dyed fabrics and home textiles, and exports to the Americas, Europe, Africa and the Middle East. He has been non-executive chairman since 2011, and his son Amit Agrawal runs the company as vice chairman and MD.
interesting_fact: The company says its denim business made it India's largest denim manufacturer. It produces 400-500 fabric designs a month in a vertically integrated operation with about 3,000 staff.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a medical doctor (MD in medicine) before spending 40 years in textiles. He sits on the advisory board of Gujarat's Textile Committee, is vice chairman of the Agrasen Foundation and Maharaja Agrasen Vidhyalaya, and has represented the Gujarat government at summits in the UK, China, Italy, Hong Kong and Singapore.
notes: Not to be confused with the steel and power Jindal family (JSW/Jindal Steel); this is a separate Ahmedabad textile company. Day-to-day leadership sits with his son Amit Agrawal (MD). Only the generic company email is published.

name: Peter Juhas
current_role: Chief Financial Officer, AerCap Holdings N.V. (NYSE: AER), Dublin
profile: Peter Juhas has been CFO of AerCap, the world's largest aircraft lessor, since April 2017, after joining as deputy CFO in 2015. Before that he was AIG's Global Head of Strategic Planning, where he worked on the 2014 sale of ILFC to AerCap. Earlier he spent 11 years as a Morgan Stanley investment banker and was an M&A lawyer at Sullivan & Cromwell. His wealth comes from executive pay and AerCap equity.
interesting_fact: At Morgan Stanley he was lead advisor to the Federal Reserve Bank and U.S. Treasury on the 2008 AIG restructuring, and on placing Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac into conservatorship.
deep_cut_fact: Long before becoming its CFO, he led AerCap's own 2006 IPO as a Morgan Stanley banker. He then helped sell AIG's ILFC to AerCap in 2014, the deal that made AerCap the industry giant.
notes: Corporate executive (not a founder). He has a Harvard A.B. in economics and a Harvard J.D. Media enquiries go through AerCap corporate communications (Dublin). The best route is probably IR, since he is the CFO.

name: Eric H. L. So
current_role: Co-founder and Director, Helus Pharma Inc. (formerly Cybin Inc.; Nasdaq/Cboe CA: HELP). In Oct 2026 he moved from executive chair/interim CEO to a board-only seat.
profile: Eric So co-founded Cybin in 2019 with Paul Glavine. Cybin develops psychedelic-derived serotonin-pathway drugs for depression and anxiety and rebranded as Helus Pharma in 2026. He was executive chairman and president, and returned as interim CEO in April 2026. In October 2026 he stepped back to the board as Mark Lawson became independent chair, ahead of Phase 3 data for HLP003.
interesting_fact: Helus's lead program, HLP003, holds FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation, and pivotal Phase 3 data is expected in Q4 2026.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a lawyer (LLB), not a scientist. Before Cybin he was VP Strategy and General Counsel at Synergex Corp (2006-2010), and he co-founded the boutique merchant bank Trinity Venture Partners.
notes: Cybin's legal name became Helus Pharma Inc. on 1 Oct 2026. His step-back to the board comes from a secondary news site (Panabee, 27 Oct 2026); confirm on ir.helus.com, which blocked automated fetch. The deep-cut career details come from MarketScreener, an aggregator. Some company bios called him a chemist, which conflicts with his LLB.

name: Adam J Katz
current_role: Co-Founder and CIO, Irenic Capital Management LP (activist hedge fund, New York); CEO and director, Irenic Acquisition Corp. (SPAC)
profile: Adam Katz spent 2013-2021 at Elliott Management, then co-founded the activist fund Irenic Capital in 2021 (about $2.5bn AUM as of March 2026). Irenic's campaign at Barnes Group put him on its board in 2024, before Apollo bought Barnes for $3.6bn (closed Jan 2025). In 2026 he launched an aerospace and defense-focused SPAC and pushed for changes at Snap and Big Yellow.
interesting_fact: Institutional Investor named him one of its ten 'Hedge Fund Rising Stars' in 2023. He holds an HBS MBA (Baker Scholar) and a Harvard JD.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating from Harvard in 2007 he co-launched the women's e-commerce company FabFitFun, later backed by Kleiner Perkins, NEA and Upfront Ventures. He kept running it through 2011 while earning his MBA and JD.
notes: His Barnes Group directorship ended when Apollo acquired the company in Jan 2025; he is also on the boards of Arconic (since 2023) and KX Topco. Irenic's website has no published contact. The best route is likely the Irenic SPAC's SEC filings, or press contacts named in Irenic campaign releases.
